personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast. (The CPCB AQI is a 24-hour average, so the AQI forecasts themselves cannot tell which hour of the day is cleaner.) WHO advises planning when and where to be active to reduce exposure [5].

personal.best_how: How is this calculated? We take the hourly PM2.5 and PM10 measured at this station in the 28 days before this hour (no later data), find the median for each hour of the day, and compare 3-hour blocks between 6 am and 9 pm with the worst 3-hour block of the day. A time is shown only if it is at least 20% cleaner and each of those hours has measurements on at least 20 of the 28 days. It is a typical pattern, not a forecast.
